_about: Owner: writer of batch B3b (concepts/paged-kv-cache, code/entrypoints-llm, code/sampling-params, code/engine-pyi, code/block-manager-hpp, code/outputs-hpp).

free-list.short: The list of KV blocks that no sequence uses. In DeepInfer it is a doubly linked list: allocate takes the first block, and a freed block goes to the end.
free-list.long: The links are stored inside a std::vector, one entry per block ({{cite csrc/engine/block_manager.hpp:27-35}}).

ref-count.short: The number of sequences that use a block. A block goes back to the free list only when its reference count is 0.
ref-count.long: Blocks::block::ref_count ({{cite csrc/engine/block_manager.hpp:105-111}}). Only forked sequences make it larger than 1.

forked-sequence.short: A new sequence that starts from the KV blocks of an existing sequence. It shares the full blocks and gets a copy of the last, partly filled block.
forked-sequence.long: Made by Scheduler.fork_seq ({{cite csrc/engine/scheduler.hpp:1061-1122}}). In this release only examples/benchmark.py calls it.

slot-mapping.short: An int32 tensor with one entry per new cache entry. Each value is the row in the paged cache where a kernel writes that entry, or -1 for no write.
slot-mapping.long: Built from the block table: block_table[i / per_block] × per_block + i % per_block ({{cite csrc/engine/input_metadata/prepare_tensor_input_v4.cpp:60}}).

prefix-caching.short: Reuse of the KV cache of an earlier request that has the same first tokens. DeepInfer's release does not include it; the docs describe an external KV cache system.
prefix-caching.long: The README lists "A KV cache system" as not included ({{cite README.md:40}}).

type-stub.short: A Python file that lists the classes and functions of a module, with types, but no code. Editors and type checkers read it. DeepInfer has one for each C++ submodule.
type-stub.long: make stubgen makes them with pybind11-stubgen ({{cite scripts/gen_stub.sh:11-13}}).

gil.short: Global Interpreter Lock: only one thread at a time runs Python code. C++ code can release it while it works, so other Python threads can run.

output-handle.short: A uint64 number that is the memory address of a C++ RequestOutput object in the pool. step() returns an array of them. Clone the object before the next step.
